correctness.rationale: Exact weighted monomial matrix obtained by polar integration; normalized Beta radial layer converges to a Gamma density in L¹ for α>-1. Subcritical phase tends to a constant, critical phase is exactly u^{ikβ}, and supercritical phase has derivative growing like log(n)^{γ-1}, giving nonstationary cancellation. An explicit diagonal unitary removes the common rotating factor; convergence of finitely many band weights gives compactness, then norm approximation extends to every continuous f. Hardy Toeplitz Fredholm theory gives exact spectrum, norm and index. The critical Gamma characteristic function never vanishes; standalone 15 numerical tests corroborate but do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The class comprises bounded angular spirals without continuous boundary trace, so the fate of spectral angular information under increasing winding is a natural Bergman localization question. The theorem gives a sharp exponent threshold, a nontrivial asymmetric log-Gamma circle convolution at criticality, a complete compactness criterion and computable essential spectral data for all real weights α>-1; the Gaussian Fock analog has a genuinely different radial fluctuation law. The finding makes the exact critical response of the first angular character explicit.
